situation:
You are the financial analyst for LARKSPUR OUTFITTERS, a specialty retailer of hiking and camping gear with eleven stores in one state. The president (judge) has asked you to recommend what the company should do with the four million dollars of idle cash sitting in its operating account, now that the first two out-of-state stores have been approved.

LARKSPUR OUTFITTERS built that cash over six profitable years, and its treasury policy keeps idle funds in accounts that pay very little but can be drawn within thirty days. New reporting software tracks each store's daily sales and cash position, so the president (judge) can see exactly which stores produced the balance.

The two new stores would cost about three and a half million dollars to open. Paying for them out of the idle cash avoids interest entirely and, by the company's own estimate, returns the money in a little under four years. To free the last of it, the board would suspend the annual profit-sharing contribution to employee retirement accounts for two years — the same contribution the veteran staff at the eleven existing stores earned that cash with.

A regional bank has offered a loan covering the full expansion at a rate the company can afford. Borrowing protects the profit-sharing contribution and leaves the idle cash where the treasury policy puts it, but the interest raises what the new stores must earn before they pay back, and the bank will not release funds until spring, delaying both openings by a season.

The president (judge) wants your analysis and your recommendation, and you will present them in the president's office. The president (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After your presentation and your answers to the president's questions, the president (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the president of LARKSPUR OUTFITTERS, the specialty hiking and camping retailer described above. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You want the financial analyst to compare paying for the two new stores out of the idle cash against borrowing the full expansion from the regional bank, to show what each does to the payback on the new stores and to the profit-sharing contribution, and to recommend one.

After the presentation you will ask these two questions:
judgeQuestions: Who carries the cost of the plan you are recommending?
How would you explain that to the employees at the older stores?
